testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

unverified.claim: The new `|| name !== id` in places() closes more self-import-under-another-name paths than the one refused case pins (member write): the old condition also missed Object.assign(CFG, …), `const o = CFG; o.ms = …` and `CFG.__proto__ = …` on a self-import read as C.ms. These three are now refused but no test pins them on their own. The mutant is still killed by the one pinned case, so this is a coverage nicety, not a defect.
unverified.evidence: I appended a PROBE test to the copy that runs sweep() on a self-import `import { CFG as C } from "./x.mjs"; export const CFG = {ms:20_000};` read as C.ms. At the PR head, assignSelf gives reaches ['reads process.env.TICKETLESS_TIMEOUT'], bindSelf gives ['reads C.ms: CFG is bound to another name …'] and protoSelf gives ['reads C.ms: CFG.__proto__ is written …']. With the old condition `if (home !== ref.mod)`, assignSelf, bindSelf and protoSelf each give [true,[],[]], so all three were accepted unseen. These cases also refuse at the PR head: reverse (read CFG, write C), another module writing under the same or another name, a namespace self-import, two aliases, and a dynamic import. The in-range write stays accepted.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optional: add `Object.assign(CFG, …)` and `const o = CFG` self-import rows to the refusedFor list next to the new member-write row.

unverified.claim: The new self-import refuse case kills three mutants of the tracer's `|| name !== id` clause (revert, `&&`, name-only). The `true` mutant survives, which the code comment itself says is equivalent.
unverified.evidence: red: node --test tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs → exit 1, fail 1 incl 'the sweep refuses a gh timeout written in the module that declares an object or in one that imports it' (revert, `&&` and name-only mutants); baseline: node --test tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs → exit 0, tests 26 pass 26 fail 0 cancelled 0, that test pass. `if (true)` mutant → exit 0, 26/26 pass, so it survives. The comment says a duplicate reason is dropped, so it is equivalent.
